question: Your team's agent includes a scaffold-module skill, defined in .claude/skills/ with a SKILL.md file, that generates boilerplate for new service modules from template files. While an engineer was exploring a legacy codebase, the skill ran a Bash command that removed an old module directory that it judged obsolete. The skill only needs to read templates and write new files. Which configuration change most directly restricts what the skill can do while it executes?

options.text: Add context: fork to the SKILL.md frontmatter so that the skill runs in an isolated sub-agent and its output stays out of the main conversation.
options.reason: The guide says context: fork isolates skill output from the main session; it does not limit which tools the skill can use, so Bash would still be available.

options.text: Convert the skill into a project-scoped slash command in .claude/commands/ so that the team shares it through version control.
options.reason: The guide says .claude/commands/ makes commands available team-wide via version control; this changes sharing, and it adds no tool restriction like allowed-tools does.

options.text: Add allowed-tools to the SKILL.md frontmatter, listing only Read, Glob, and Write so that Bash cannot be used during skill execution.
options.reason: The guide states that allowed-tools in skill frontmatter restricts tool access during skill execution, for example limiting it to file write operations to prevent destructive actions.

options.text: Copy the skill into ~/.claude/skills/ under a different name so that each engineer runs a personal variant without affecting teammates.
options.reason: The guide describes personal variants in ~/.claude/skills/ as a way to customize without affecting teammates; this changes scope, not the tools available during execution.
